name: Subway Platform
desc: A station platform running away into the tunnel — a gum-pocked deck with a band of tactile blister studs and a painted line at the lip, the coping edge dropping away into the ballast trough where two rails run out to the dark — and a train's headlamp swelling somewhere down the tunnel, throwing its light up the rails and along the platform before it fades again.

energy.doc: how hard the headlamp burns down the tunnel and how much light the platform holds

scale.doc: perspective spread of the platform — deck, studs and trough all follow it

density.doc: how fine the tactile studs, ballast, sleepers and blowing litter are

grime.doc: trodden gum, scuff and the general filth of a working platform

speed.doc: how often the trains come and how fast the light drifts

hue.doc: platform-light / edge-line hue (44 = warm sodium and yellow paint; the deck and trough answer cold on the complement)

x.doc: vanishing point x — the platform and trough both run to it

y.doc: horizon line y (the mouth of the tunnel) — nothing is ever painted above it

alpha.doc: opacity of the headlamp, platform light and haze

style.doc: concrete: a working platform — raw worn deck, yellow line, blister studs, sodium light, gum trodden into everything · deco: a 1930s station, patterned tilework laid into the deck, warm and ornamented · disused: abandoned — no trains ever come, the rails gone to rust, cold and silent · diagram: the station abandons the world entirely and becomes its own transit map — flat colour bars and blank geometry, no material at all

act.doc: service: an ordinary timetable, a train every so often · rush: they come one after another · nightshift: long empty stretches, the platform mostly waiting

seed.doc: deterministic seed for ballast, gum, scuff and litter
